name: Ellora Caves & Kailasa Temple
builder: Buddhist, Hindu and Jain patrons; Kailasa under the Rashtrakutas
overview:
The Ellora Caves, near Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar in Maharashtra, form one of the world's greatest rock-cut complexes, stretching for about two kilometres along a basalt escarpment. There are 34 caves in all, carved between roughly the 6th and 10th centuries CE, and they are unusual because they hold Buddhist, Hindu and Jain monuments side by side, reflecting a long tradition of religious coexistence. The Buddhist caves are the earliest, followed by the Hindu caves, many linked to the Rashtrakuta dynasty, and then the Jain caves.

The beauty and drama of Ellora lie in its sculpture and scale. The jewel is Cave 16, the Kailasa Temple, a full-sized temple carved from a single rock, cut downward from the top of the hillside, with a gateway, courtyard, hall, shrine and tower all sculpted from the living stone. It is traditionally linked to the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I in the 8th century and is dedicated to Shiva, imitating Mount Kailash. Its walls are crowded with scenes from the Ramayana and Mahabharata and large figures of elephants and lions.

Other caves reward careful exploration. Cave 10, the Vishvakarma Cave, is a Buddhist chaitya hall with a high ribbed ceiling that resembles wooden beams, and a large Buddha in front of a stupa. Cave 12, Teen Tal, is a three-storey Buddhist monastery. Among the Hindu caves, Cave 15, Cave 21 and Cave 29 hold powerful carvings of Shiva and Vishnu. The Jain group, including Cave 32, the Indra Sabha, has finely detailed ceilings and sculpture.

Ellora was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983. It is famous for the Kailasa Temple, regarded as one of the largest monolithic rock excavations in the world, and as an example of artistic and religious harmony.

Visitors should allow half a day or more, wear comfortable shoes and avoid midday heat. The site is close to the Grishneshwar Jyotirlinga, Daulatabad Fort and Khuldabad, and Ajanta is a longer day trip. Check current opening days and ticket rules with official sources.
